verdict: M&T Bank earned $775M — profit slipped 2% from a year ago as it set aside a bit more for possible loan losses, while its core lending income held steady.

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest on loans minus what M&T pays depositors — the core earnings engine of a regional bank.

segments.name: Noninterest income
segments.note: Mortgage banking, trust and service charges, card fees and other fee income.

opex.name: Salaries and employee benefits
opex.note: Pay for the bank's branch, lending and operations staff — its biggest cost.

opex.name: Other noninterest expense
opex.note: Technology and data processing, professional services, occupancy, FDIC assessments and everything else.

otherDetail: A bank's statement runs straight from revenue, credit costs and expenses to pre-tax income of $1,008M.

takeaways.title: The core engine is steady
takeaways.text: Net interest income rose 2% to $1.8B — loan and deposit balances are growing slowly, and the taxable-equivalent margin held up.

takeaways.title: Credit is a watch item, not a problem
takeaways.text: The provision for credit losses rose to $135M from $125M a year ago — a modest build as the loan book grows, and the main reason profit dipped despite steady revenue.

takeaways.title: EPS held up better than profit
takeaways.text: Diluted EPS was $5.04 on $732M available to common shareholders; buybacks keep shrinking the share count, cushioning small profit declines.

footerNote: For a bank, the provision for credit losses plays the role of cost of revenue. Net income was $775M; after preferred dividends, $732M was available to common shareholders. M&T reports revenue on a taxable-equivalent basis of $1,805M for net interest income in some tables; this page uses the GAAP figures.
